title: Dominion Dynamics deep company and capability profile

selectedGap.reason: User-directed deep research cycle for Dominion Dynamics and its Canadian Arctic autonomy, sensing, command-and-control, aerospace, simulation, and procurement-intelligence portfolio.

candidates.reviewerRationale: Dominion Dynamics is worthy of inclusion because its canonical site, official newsroom, company-issued releases, live AURION service, and a current Government of Canada founder profile establish a substantial Ottawa-based Canadian defence-technology company with four distinct public capability families: AuraNet data fusion and command and control, the Scout Autonomous Collaborative Platform, sovereign AI simulation with Denvr, and AURION procurement intelligence. The evidence also supports a Kanata manufacturing facility, Toronto development office, current financing-backed scale-up, public contact path, and operator-facing Arctic field activity. Reviewers should verify whether AURION belongs inside the same defence-prime profile, whether Scout should remain program-level until specifications mature, and how prominently to present Operation NANOOK-NUNALIVUT activity because the deployment evidence located here is company-reported rather than an independent Government of Canada confirmation. No exact facility address or independently verified legal name was found in the canonical sources used, so those details remain omitted.

fieldEvidence.excerpt: Dominion's canonical site describes an integrated Canadian defence portfolio combining autonomy, sensing, communications, command and control, data fusion, edge processing, and modular integration for remote and infrastructure-constrained operations.

The official platform page says AuraNet combines imagery, signals, telemetry, and structured reporting in an integrated command-and-control and data-fusion layer that can connect with existing architectures.

Dominion's announcement describes an uncrewed collaborative aircraft intended to extend crewed-fighter reach and support surveillance, electronic warfare, strike support, and high-risk or remote operations within a broader command architecture.

The corrected Dominion-Denvr release describes a Canadian-controlled AI simulation environment for developing, training, and validating Autonomous Collaborative Platforms on Denvr's sovereign Canada AI Platform.

Dominion's official AURION page documents a normalized intelligence layer linking procurement records, contract lifecycles, companies, departments, funding, lobbying, supplier status, and active opportunities.

The March 2026 company release commits an initial $50 million to engineering, prototyping, simulation, and advisory work for a sovereign Canadian Autonomous Collaborative Platform later identified publicly as Scout.

Dominion's field account says its self-funded eight-week engagement equipped three long-range patrols operating with Canadian Rangers and used AuraNet for tracking, communications, a common picture, and operator-driven iteration.
Dominion and Denvr publicly announced a partnership to build a sovereign AI simulation environment for Autonomous Collaborative Platforms using the Canadian-controlled Canada AI Platform.

Dominion reports that Canadian Rangers used AuraNet and lightweight sensing and communications equipment during a self-funded Operation NANOOK-NUNALIVUT field engagement; this is company-reported activity rather than independent government confirmation.

The current financing release identifies a 25,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Kanata, Ontario, and a Toronto development office; the earlier launch release identifies company headquarters in Ottawa.
Dominion's canonical site publishes info@ddc2.com and links its newsroom, careers board, LinkedIn, YouTube, and X profiles.

The Government of Canada identifies Eliot Pence as Dominion's founder and describes the company as a Canadian defence-technology firm focused on sovereign aerospace, autonomy, and command-and-control capability.

Dominion's June 2026 release says the company is using its Series A to accelerate AuraNet and Scout, grow its workforce, operate from a new Kanata manufacturing facility, and expand through a Toronto development office.
The company announced a $139 million CAD Series A led by Georgian and reported total financing of $169 million CAD since its 2025 launch.

Analyst mapping: a field-tested common operating picture that combines patrol tracking, sensing, communications, and ground conditions is strongly relevant to Arctic Domain Awareness, without implying a government procurement decision or endorsement.

Analyst mapping: the official description of onboard sensing, edge models, local processing, and constrained-environment data fusion supports an Edge Data Processing alignment, subject to deployment-specific architecture review.

Analyst mapping: an uncrewed collaborative aircraft intended for persistent surveillance in remote and contested areas plausibly supports Autonomous Patrol and Monitoring, but public prototype maturity and mission configuration require review.

Analyst mapping: Dominion explicitly positions the ACP for remote Arctic operations and expanded sensing reach, making Arctic Domain Awareness a plausible future alignment rather than a verified deployed outcome.

profileData.mandate: Build sovereign Canadian defence technology for extreme and infrastructure-constrained operations, beginning with an Arctic autonomy stack and the digital backbone for next-generation command and control.
profileData.operatingModel: The company publicly emphasizes modular, interoperable, AI-native systems, operator co-development, rapid field iteration, Canadian-controlled infrastructure, and complementary software, sensing, communications, aerospace, and data products.
profileData.history: Founded by Eliot Pence and publicly launched in 2025 as an Ottawa-headquartered Canadian defence-technology company. The Government of Canada describes Dominion as working to establish sovereign aerospace, autonomy, and command-and-control capability.
profileData.portfolioScope: AuraNet common-operating-picture and data-fusion software; Arctic sensing and communications integration; Scout autonomous collaborative aircraft; sovereign AI simulation and validation with Denvr; and AURION public procurement, supplier, contract, funding, and government-relationship intelligence.
profileData.canadianFootprint: Ottawa headquarters and a 25,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Kanata, Ontario, plus a Toronto development office disclosed in the June 2026 financing announcement.
profileData.publicContact: Canonical company contact: info@ddc2.com. The official site also links the company newsroom, careers board, LinkedIn, YouTube, and X accounts.
profileData.currentActivity: The June 2026 Series A announcement says Dominion is accelerating AuraNet and Scout, growing its team to more than 100, operating from its new Kanata manufacturing facility, and expanding development activity in Toronto.
profileData.financing: Dominion announced a $139 million CAD Series A led by Georgian in June 2026 and reported total capital raised of $169 million CAD since launch.
profileData.evidencePosture: Official company product and newsroom evidence is strong and current, with Government of Canada corroboration for company identity and founder. Operation NANOOK-NUNALIVUT activity is company-reported and should not be presented as government endorsement, procurement, or independently verified operational effectiveness.
